scope: Three parallel fixed-state H-alpha transport investigations after PR 13; no population, temperature, wind or observational refit.
primary_state: The saved eight-cell atmosphere at the refined +5.127 percent mass-loss point used by PRs 12 and 13.
questions: Does finite spherical geometry reduce absorption of H-alpha emitted by other cells relative to the plane-parallel closure?
Does the actual radial velocity field, or a separately labeled differential-velocity probe, reduce receiver-frame H-alpha absorption?
After explicitly including reverse recycling, which channels can remove an H-alpha photon from the H-alpha/Ly-beta cycle?

geometry: Use the same opacity, emissivity, shell edges and spectral measure in the slab and sphere.
Separate lower LTE cells, other inner emitters, the receiver itself, outer emitters and continuum.
Check photon balance and source superposition to relative tolerance 1e-9.
Record angle and frequency refinements against a one-percent target for the primary receiver.
velocity: Shift both emitting and absorbing profiles along each ray.
Check the zero-velocity static limit and common frequency/velocity translation.
Separate the actual radial flow from hypothetical 5.5 and 13 km/s differential probes.
Record angle, frequency and segment refinements against a one-percent target for the primary receiver.
conversion: Do not count the 3p-to-1s radiative branch as irreversible H-alpha destruction.
Include the reverse recycling path and explicitly state terminal outcomes.
Check nonnegative normalized probabilities, conservation and transparent/trapped limiting cases.
Audit any saved rate-ledger state against the primary state before combining numbers.

interpretation_rules: A fixed-state reduction of pumping does not by itself predict a proportional change in the line source function.
The ordinary rate closure does not already contain the complete emitted intercell H-alpha field. Suppressing an added field does not establish improvement over that baseline.
Absorption measured using net extinction includes stimulated emission and is not automatically a gross microscopic excitation rate.
A single-flight continuum destruction fraction does not bound destruction after repeated scattering.
A successful diagnostic does not establish a new self-consistent atmosphere or a better fit after the common observation operator.
Preserve unsuccessful controls and distinguish incomplete execution from a valid failed scientific criterion.
